subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Pension Fund Choice Overload
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Pension Fund Choice Overload.

hook.text: A company offered 59 pension fund options. Enrollment dropped. When reduced to 5 curated options, participation rose 10.

buildup.text: Too many investment options paralyze retirement savers. The fear of making the wrong choice leads to making no choice.

discovery.text: Iyengar and Kamenica showed each additional 10 funds offered reduced participation by 2%.

twist.text: Target-date funds solve this. One fund that automatically adjusts risk over time gives a sensible default.

climax.text: Good retirement policy simplifies choice. Fewer, well-designed options outperform a marketplace of hundreds that nobody.

punchline.text: Fewer pension options means more people saving for retirement.

quiz.question: How does reducing pension fund options affect participation?
options: It decreases participation because people want more choice
It increases participation by reducing choice paralysis
It has no effect on enrollment rates

details.summary: Offering too many pension fund options paralyzes decision-making, causing people to either avoid choosing entirely or pick poorly. Reducing options, providing a well-designed default fund, and offering guided decision tools improve both participation and outcomes.
details.whyItMatters: Retirement savings affect lifelong financial security, yet many pension systems overwhelm participants with dozens of fund options they are not equipped to evaluate. Simplifying this choice architecture can improve millions of retirement outcomes.
takeaways: More fund options reduce participation rates rather than improving them
Well-designed default funds capture most participants and perform well
Guided choice tools help the few who want to choose actively

faq.question: Why does having more fund options reduce pension participation?
faq.answer: Each additional fund option increases comparison difficulty. People who cannot confidently evaluate options procrastinate indefinitely rather than risk choosing wrong. Participation drops by roughly 2 percent for every 10 additional fund options offered.

faq.question: What makes a good default pension fund?
faq.answer: Target-date funds that automatically adjust risk based on the participant's age are the most common and effective defaults. They require no ongoing decisions, provide age-appropriate diversification, and perform well for the average saver.
